screening_results.reason: Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging), I3 (functional imaging), I4 (executive function tasks). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (healthy human participants) — study sample comprises individuals with autistic spectrum disorder (clinical population), not healthy adults, so it does not meet the review population requirement.

English peer-reviewed neuroimaging study using both fMRI and PET, employing the Tower of London task (an executive function/planning task). No exclusion criteria are met; full-text review warranted to confirm participant details and methods.

The abstract describes an English peer-reviewed PET neuroimaging study in healthy human volunteers examining executive function (WCST). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are present.

fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (an executive function task) published in NeuroImage (English). Imaging modality and task domain meet inclusion. Participant health status not specified in abstract, so full-text needed to confirm I2 (healthy humans). No exclusion criteria met.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human adults examining an executive function (attentional switching/allocation within working memory). No exclusion criteria are met and the abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study in human participants examining executive function (working memory/reading span). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract indicates healthy adult groups (high- vs low-span). Include for full-text review.

Abstract indicates fMRI of the Tower of London (an executive function task) in a peer-reviewed English journal, but does not clearly state that participants were healthy adults (mentions TBI in background). Insufficient information on sample health status — include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English, peer-reviewed neuroimaging study) and I4 (examined executive function tasks). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participants are migraine patients plus controls—not exclusively healthy adults) and I3 (used structural MRI/VBM, not fMRI or PET task activation).

English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=11) examining the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, a canonical executive function/cognitive control task. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.
English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human adults examining an executive function task (random number generation). Abstract meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study examining executive control (SART) and related activations; participants are human but abstract does not explicitly state they were healthy. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human adults examining working memory subcomponents (maintenance, retrieval, manipulation), which are executive functions. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract activation data for meta-analysis.

Meets inclusion criteria: peer-reviewed English neuroimaging study (NeuroImage), healthy human participants, PET modality using [11C]raclopride, and examines executive function (Montreal Card Sorting Task). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract clearly meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study (NeuroImage) in healthy human adults examining working memory/executive function with motivational manipulation. No exclusion criteria (non-human or non-English) are met. Recommend inclusion for full-text review.

Abstract reports an English-language PET neuroimaging study of executive function tasks in humans, meeting I1, I3, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy (I2 not demonstrated); no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health and other details.

Study focuses on people with prodromal/at-risk mental state (clinical population), not healthy adults, so it does not meet inclusion criterion I2. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging article) and I4 (examines executive function/working memory). Inclusion not met or not demonstrated: I2 (healthy participants not met) and I3 (modality fMRI/PET not demonstrated in abstract). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.

English-language PET meta-analysis in healthy human participants that includes cognitive tasks (reasoning, mental calculation, spatial working memory) relevant to executive function. The abstract emphasizes rest>task contrasts rather than task activations, so full-text review is needed to confirm it reports executive function task activations.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy adult humans examining executive function tasks (inhibition and working memory). No exclusion criteria met; all inclusion criteria are satisfied based on the abstract.

Peer-reviewed English neuroimaging study using PET that includes healthy human participants (84 controls) and examines executive function/working memory tasks (N-back, one-back, Wisconsin Card Sorting, etc.). Although the abstract reports PET activation differences in patients rather than controls, the study meets inclusion criteria and activation data for healthy adults may be present in full text; include for full-text review.

Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed neuroimaging publication (NeuroImage), healthy human participants ('normal subjects'), uses fMRI, and examines executive function/cognitive control (emotional linguistic go/no-go response inhibition). No exclusion criteria evident in abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (healthy human participants), I4 (executive function task: WCST). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 and I3—this study used rTMS (neuromodulation) rather than fMRI or PET neuroimaging, so it does not satisfy the required neuroimaging study criterion. Therefore exclude.

Participants are patients with mania (not healthy), so I2 (healthy participants) is not met. The study is an English peer-reviewed article (I1) and examines an affective go/no-go executive task (I4). Imaging modality (fMRI/PET) is not specified in the abstract (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.

Published in an English peer-reviewed journal (NeuroImage) using simultaneous fMRI and EEG in human participants performing a central executive task (free-paced repeated subtraction) relevant to executive function/working memory. No exclusion criteria are met; inclusion criteria appear satisfied though participant health status/age is not explicitly stated in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm details.

fMRI study using the n-back (working memory/executive) task, published in English. Meets I1, I3, and I4. Unclear from abstract whether results for healthy control participants are reported separately or whether the sample is exclusively healthy, so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Meets inclusion criteria: English-language peer-reviewed neuroimaging study (abstract/DOI present), healthy adult participants (7 normal adults), uses fMRI, and examines executive function (set-shifting on Trail Making Test). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Study is English peer-reviewed fMRI research of executive function and includes an age- and IQ-matched healthy control group. However, the abstract does not clearly state whether control-group activations are reported separately for meta-analysis. Include for full-text review to confirm usable healthy-adult activation data.

No healthy participants: study examines response inhibition in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder, so inclusion criterion I2 (healthy human participants) is not met. Inclusion met: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (executive function/cognitive control task). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) are met.

fMRI study examining working memory (an executive function) that includes healthy control participants. However, participants also include moderate–severe TBI patients and the abstract does not state whether healthy-adult activations are separable. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English-language peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human volunteers examining executive function tasks (N-back working memory and verbal fluency). No exclusion criteria met; abstract provides sufficient detail for inclusion in full-text review.

Study is an English-language peer-reviewed fMRI study examining working memory (n-back), an executive function task, and includes healthy control participants. No exclusion criteria are met. Abstract provides sufficient relevance for inclusion for full-text review to extract activation data from healthy adults.

Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human adults examining executive functions (go/no-go and WCST). No exclusion criteria met; abstract describes methods and participant population sufficiently for inclusion for full-text review.

PET study in English examining working memory (an executive function) in human adults; meets I1,I3,I4. Participant health is ambiguous because they are classified by hypertensive status, so I2 is unclear from the abstract. Include for full-text review to determine health status and eligibility.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function task) in heavy cannabis users; fMRI and executive task criteria met. However, participant 'healthy adults' status is unclear because subjects are heavy cannabis users, so inclusion on that criterion is uncertain from the abstract. No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine whether participants meet the 'healthy adults' requirement.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants examining executive function (attentional set-shifting). No exclusion criteria met; abstract clearly reports task-related prefrontal activations relevant to executive control.

No exclusion criteria met. Meets I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (verbal working memory = executive task). Does NOT meet I2: participants are described as depressed patients (post-antidepressant therapy), not healthy adults, so study is excluded from a meta-analysis of healthy adult executive-function activations.

Published in English in a peer-reviewed journal (I1), uses fMRI (I3), and examines executive function (Go/Nogo) tasks (I4). The abstract does not explicitly state that participants were healthy humans (I2 unclear), so include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Participants are patients with schizophrenia, not healthy adults (I2 not met). Study is English-language and uses fMRI (I1, I3 met). It reports a social cognition paradigm and associations with executive function, but it does not clearly use an executive function task (I4 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.

Peer-reviewed English fMRI study reporting data from 15 healthy matched control participants who performed the n-Back (verbal working memory) task — an executive function paradigm. Although MS patients are included, healthy adult control activations are reported and fMRI methods are used, so the study meets inclusion criteria and warrants full-text review to extract healthy adult task activations.

Abstract meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed NeuroImage article (I1), healthy human adults (n=18) (I2), fMRI study (I3), and examines an executive function task (Tower of London) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

Participants are multiple sclerosis patients (not healthy adults) so inclusion criterion I2 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging), I3 (fMRI), I4 (working memory—a cognitive/executive task). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore exclude due to failure to meet I2 (healthy participants).

EXCLUDED because participants are adults with ADHD (inclusion criterion I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English-language peer-reviewed neuroimaging), I3 (functional imaging implied), I4 (examines executive function). Exclusion criteria met: none. I2 (healthy participants) not demonstrated and is clearly not met.

Study examines neural responses to psychosocial stress, not executive function or cognitive control tasks. No exclusion criteria met (E1,E2). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (participant health not specified), I4 (does not examine executive function tasks).

Peer-reviewed English fMRI study using a memory-guided saccade task (spatial working memory), comparing high-risk offspring and matched healthy controls. Meets I1, I3, and I4 and includes healthy human participants (HC), but primary sample includes high-risk subjects so it's unclear if healthy-adult activation maps alone are reported—include for full-text review to resolve.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (examines working memory/executive function). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (healthy participants) — study involves persons with multiple sclerosis, not healthy adults, so exclude.

Study examines working memory dysfunction in schizophrenia (patients), not healthy participants. Inclusion: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (working memory/executive task) are met. Inclusion I2 (healthy human participants) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.
English peer-reviewed fMRI study in humans using a go/no-go inhibitory control task (executive function); no exclusion criteria met based on abstract.

Published in Neuropsychologia (English, peer-reviewed) using fMRI and explicitly examining executive/cognitive control tasks (switching, inhibition). Abstract does not specify participant health status (healthy adults not explicitly stated), so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

This is an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants that examines executive control (Stroop interference and DLPFC activity). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are present; full text review is appropriate.

English-language peer-reviewed fMRI study (Neuropsychology) with 11 human participants (no patient population indicated), uses fMRI, and examines n-back working memory tasks (executive function). No exclusion criteria met in abstract. Include for full-text review to extract activation data.
fMRI study of go/no-go response inhibition in healthy human adults published in an English peer-reviewed journal; meets executive function task criterion and all imaging/participant criteria.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study in human participants using an executive-function-related working memory task. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract; inclusion criteria (I1,I2,I3,I4) are satisfied. Include for full-text review to extract activation details.

fMRI study in humans examining phonological and visual working memory (an executive function), published in English peer-reviewed journal. Abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy, so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility (I2 not demonstrated).

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human adults examining spatial working memory, which is an executive function/cognitive control task. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract activation coordinates and task details.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study assessing visuospatial working memory (an executive function) in postmenopausal human participants receiving hormone therapy; fits neuroimaging executive-function review and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text recommended to confirm participant health status.

Abstract reports an English-language peer-reviewed NeuroImage paper using event-related fMRI and EEG to study a GO/NOGO executive control task. This satisfies I1, I3, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy (I2 not confirmed), and no exclusion criteria (non-human or non-English) are met. Recommend full-text review to confirm health status of participants.

Participants are children (ages 8–13) and include a clinical ADHD group, so the study does not address healthy adult participants required by the review objective. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (examines executive/cognitive control task). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I2 (healthy human participants — includes clinical ADHD group; additionally participants are children, not adults).

Peer-reviewed fMRI study in humans (Neuroscience) examining working memory component processes (an executive function/cognitive control domain). Abstract reports subject behavioral and fMRI measures and gives no indication of a clinical or non-healthy population; meets inclusion criteria. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status and extract activation data.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study using an executive/go-no-go task and it includes a non-violent, no-mental-illness control group (healthy participants). However, the abstract focuses on clinical groups and does not confirm that healthy adult activations/coordinates are reported separately, so full-text review is needed to confirm eligibility and extract data.

Study reports fMRI neuroimaging in an English peer-reviewed journal and examines working memory retrieval (an executive function). The abstract does not explicitly state participant health status (healthy adults), so full-text review is needed to confirm I2.

Abstract reports an English-language, peer-reviewed fMRI study using a stop-signal task (an executive/cognitive control paradigm) in human participants, but does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status and other eligibility.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in nonpsychotic human relatives (healthy participants) performing an auditory verbal working memory task requiring interference resolution, i.e., an executive function/cognitive control task. No exclusion criteria met from abstract. Full text review warranted to confirm participant health status and details.

Abstract reports an English-language peer-reviewed fMRI study in Neuropsychologia (I1), uses healthy human participants (I2), employs fMRI (I3), and investigates executive function/problem solving (Tower of London) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in 20 healthy adult human participants investigating cognitive switching, an executive function task. Meets all inclusion criteria (I1–I4); no exclusion criteria are met or indicated.

Study is an English-language fMRI paper (I1, I3 met) but investigates visual/magnocellular processing in schizophrenia patients, not executive function tasks (I4 not met) and does not consist of healthy participants only (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply.

No exclusion criteria met. However, participants are ecstasy/amphetamine users (not healthy adults), so inclusion criterion I2 (healthy human participants) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (examines executive function: working memory). Inclusion not met: I2 (healthy participants).

Study uses Turner syndrome patients (clinical population), not healthy adult participants. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1/E2 not met). Inclusion IDs met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion ID not met: I2 (healthy human participants). Therefore exclude.

fMRI study of Go/No-go response inhibition (an executive function) published in an English peer-reviewed journal. Confident on I1, I3, I4; participant health not explicitly stated in abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm I2 (healthy adults).

Participants are people with schizophrenia, not healthy adults (I2 not met). Abstract confirms English language peer-reviewed publication (I1) and use of fMRI (I3). Executive-function task status unclear (I4 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met. Exclude for review because population does not match healthy participant requirement.

Study is a structural MRI (cortical thickness) comparison of adults with ADHD and controls, not a task-based fMRI/PET activation study of executive function in healthy adults. Inclusion met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I3 (fMRI or PET), I4 (executive function task activations), and I2 (healthy participants—not clearly satisfied because primary sample is ADHD despite presence of controls). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) were met.

Participants are children with ADHD and typically developing children, not healthy adult participants. Inclusion met: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (executive function Go/No-go). Inclusion not met: I2 (healthy human participants — study involves clinical ADHD group and children, not healthy adults). Exclusion criteria none met.

Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study with healthy adult participants; examines executive resources (planning and working memory)—an executive function/cognitive control task. No exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study using a Tower of London executive function task and including a matched healthy control adult group. However, the abstract reports comparisons with an autistic group and does not confirm whether control-only activation data are reported separately; full-text review required.

PET study published in English with healthy human participants using a Tower of London planning task (an executive function/cognitive control task). Meets all inclusion criteria (I1-I4); no exclusion criteria met. Abstract provides sufficient information for inclusion for full-text review.

PET study (H2(15)O-PET) using the Tower of London planning task in healthy adults; addresses planning/executive function; published in English in peer-reviewed journal Brain. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, I4. No exclusion criteria met based on abstract.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study examining executive/control processes (meets I1, I3, I4). Participant health status (I2: healthy humans) is not explicitly stated in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm. No exclusion criteria apparent.

English-language peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human adults examining visual spatial and nonspatial working memory (an executive function). Abstract clearly meets inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

English-language, peer-reviewed fMRI study published in The Journal of Neuroscience examining S-R mapping and reaction-time tasks (CRT, GNGRT) that index executive function/cognitive control. fMRI modality and executive-task focus are clear. Participant health not specified in abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed (PNAS), healthy human participants (young and senior), PET neuroimaging, and examines executive function/task-switching in working memory. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports an English-language, peer-reviewed PET study in healthy young women using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (an executive function task). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply; include for full-text review.

fMRI study of a verbal working memory (executive function) task that includes healthy adult control participants. Exclusion criteria not met. Full text needed to confirm availability of activation data for healthy controls separate from cocaine abusers and to determine suitability for meta-analysis.

Includes fMRI and a cognitive set-shifting (executive function) task in humans and macaques (so I1, I3, I4 are satisfied). The abstract does not explicitly state that the human participants were healthy adults (I2 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria (purely non-human or non-English) are clearly met; include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract reports an English-language, peer-reviewed fMRI study using syllable working memory tasks (an executive function), so I1, I3, and I4 are met. Participant health status is not specified in the abstract (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm healthy participant status.

PET study of verbal working memory (an executive function) using PET in human subjects; matches neuroimaging and task domains. Abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy, so inclusion criterion I2 is not clearly demonstrated; no exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health and details.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study examining the psychological refractory period and executive functions; satisfies I1, I3, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy (I2 uncertain). Per screening rules, include for full-text review when participant health is not specified.

English peer-reviewed PET study in humans examining working memory (an executive function task). Meets imaging and task domains; no exclusion criteria evident. Recommend full-text for data extraction and effect sizes.

Abstract reports an English-language PET study examining executive function (MCST) and measures striatal dopamine release during task performance—meeting I1, I3, and I4. However, the abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults (I2 not demonstrated). Therefore include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

EXCLUDED: study participants are youths and include a clinical VCFS group (does not meet inclusion I2 for healthy participants relevant to a meta-analysis of healthy adults). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I2 (Healthy human participants — sample not exclusively healthy adults and includes clinical subjects; also participants are adolescents, not the target healthy adults).

PET study in English peer-reviewed journal with healthy human participants performing verbal working memory and sustained attention tasks (executive function/cognitive control). All inclusion criteria (I1, I2, I3, I4) are met and no exclusion criteria apply, so include for full-text review.

Participants are euthymic bipolar disorder patients—not healthy adults—so inclusion criterion I2 is not met. The study does meet I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), and I4 (working-memory/executive tasks). No exclusion criteria (E1, E2) are met.

English-language fMRI study investigating working memory (an executive function). Participant health status is not explicitly stated in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm healthy human participants.

No exclusion criteria met. Excluded because inclusion criterion I2 (healthy human participants) is not met: the study examines major depressive disorder patients rather than healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging), I3 (fMRI/PET), I4 (executive/inhibitory control task).

Study is an English peer-reviewed PET neuroimaging study in healthy human participants investigating visual working memory—a core executive function/cognitive control domain. No exclusion criteria (non-human or non-English) are met. Include for full-text review to extract activation data relevant to executive function meta-analysis.

No exclusion criteria met. Met inclusion criteria: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (PET neuroimaging), I4 (working memory updating = executive function). Does not meet I2: participants are PTSD patients (clinical sample), not healthy adults; therefore excluded from a meta-analysis of healthy adult executive function activations.

Study is a structural VBM investigation in remitted geriatric depression, not an fMRI or PET task-activation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging), I2 (includes healthy control participants), I4 (examines executive function via neuropsychological tests). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (does not use fMRI or PET); study involves clinical patients and does not provide healthy adult task activations required for the meta-analysis.

Peer-reviewed English fMRI study in NeuroImage examining executive function (working memory selection vs maintenance) in human participants. Meets I1, I3, I4. Participant health status not explicitly stated in abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm I2 (healthy adults).

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in human subjects performing an audiospatial n-back working-memory task (an executive function/cognitive control task). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging study in Neuropsychologia), I3 (fMRI), I4 (examines executive function — verbal working memory manipulation). Inclusion not met: I2 (healthy participants) — sample consists of adolescents and young adults with dyslexia (clinical group), so fails the 'healthy human participants' criterion.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed neuroimaging study (NeuroImage), healthy human participants (12 volunteers), PET imaging, and working memory task (executive function). No exclusion criteria are met.

fMRI study using the stop-signal task (an executive/cognitive control task) in human participants; published in an English-language peer-reviewed journal. The abstract does not explicitly state 'healthy' participants, so include for full-text review to confirm health status.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed NeuroImage fMRI study examining attention-switching within/between verbal and visuospatial working memory (an executive function). It does not state participant health status explicitly, so include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed NeuroImage article (I1); healthy human participants (n=12) (I2); uses fMRI (ASL perfusion) (I3); examines executive function/cognitive control tasks (2-back working memory and sustained attention) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed NeuroImage article (I1), healthy human volunteers (I2), PET neuroimaging (I3), and investigation of executive function tasks (working memory and planning) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met; abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study using a go/no-go (cognitive control) task in humans. I1, I3, and I4 are satisfied; participant health status not explicitly stated, so include for full-text to confirm I2. No exclusion criteria met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (English peer-reviewed neuroimaging), I3 (fMRI), I4 (cognitive control tasks). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I2 as required for this review (healthy ADULT participants) — study uses children (ADHD patients and child controls), so it does not address the meta-analysis objective of healthy adults.

Abstract reports an fMRI emotional counting Stroop paradigm in Biological Psychiatry (English) and targets anterior cingulate affective division — an executive/cognitive control task. However, the abstract does not specify participant demographics or explicitly confirm healthy adult participants, so include for full-text review to verify I2.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants examining an executive function task (Wisconsin Card Sorting Task/set shifting). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

This is an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants using n-back working memory tasks (load-dependent; emotional vocal stimuli). N-back is an executive function/cognitive control task, so it meets I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend inclusion for full-text review.

Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed journal (I1), fMRI study (I3), examines working memory using an n-back task which is an executive function/cognitive control task (I4). Participants are described as 'subjects' with no clinical population mentioned, implying healthy adults (I2). No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm participant health details and task specifics.

Peer-reviewed fMRI study (I1, I3) using n-back working memory and a gambling task targeting executive/decision processes (I4). The study includes healthy control participants, but also remitted bipolar patients and the abstract does not clarify whether separate healthy-only activation results are reported (I2 not clearly met). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to determine eligibility of healthy-adult activation data.

Meets I1 (English peer-reviewed), I2 (healthy human participants), and I3 (fMRI). The task is a motor timing/continuation tapping paradigm; abstract suggests involvement of higher cognitive/executive regions but does not clearly state an executive function/cognitive control task (I4 unclear). Include for full-text review to determine whether I4 is satisfied.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study examining a go/no-go response inhibition task (executive function). Abstract does not state whether participants were healthy adults, so I2 (healthy participants) is not confirmed from abstract alone. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health status.

Abstract examines response inhibition (an executive function), but does not specify imaging modality (fMRI/PET) or participant ages (likely developmental sample including children). Insufficient information to confirm all inclusion criteria or adult-only sample; include for full-text review.
Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human subjects examining Stop-signal response inhibition (an executive function). No exclusion criteria are met.

fMRI study in English peer-reviewed journal with 30 healthy human participants performing an n-back spatial working memory task (an executive function/cognitive control task); no exclusion criteria met.

PET study in English peer-reviewed journal testing controlled updating of verbal working memory in 10 normal (healthy) adults — an executive function task. Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria met.

Peer-reviewed English fMRI study in Neuropsychologia with healthy participants (hearing native signers). Uses a hybrid fMRI design and an n-back task assessing working memory/episodic buffer, which is an executive function/cognitive control task. No exclusion criteria met from abstract.

English peer-reviewed fMRI study using an emotional Stroop (a cognitive control/executive function task) that reports activations for control (healthy) participants. The abstract does not make clear whether healthy adult data are reported in extractable form for meta-analysis, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an English peer-reviewed fMRI study of executive/cognitive control tasks in human participants across adolescence and adulthood. It appears to use healthy subjects but adult-only activation data or separable adult results are not explicit, so include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract reports fMRI data from healthy subjects examining visual working memory (an executive function), is an English peer-reviewed neuroimaging study, and includes functional MRI analyses of task-related connectivity; therefore meets inclusion criteria and should be included for full-text review.

Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants examining executive function (Go/No-Go behavioural inhibition) and cognitive control. No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to extract activation data.

Meets all inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study in Neuropsychologia (I1), healthy human participants (17 right-handed subjects) (I2), uses fMRI (I3), and examines executive function/planning using the Tower of London task (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Full-text review appropriate to extract activation coordinates and details for meta-analysis.

Meets inclusion criteria: English peer-reviewed fMRI study examining an executive/cognitive control task (n-back) and includes healthy human control participants. No exclusion criteria met. Abstract reports activations for both groups; full text needed to extract healthy-control activation coordinates/contrasts for meta-analysis.

PET study in English (Neuroscience Letters) examining visuospatial N-Back (working memory/executive) and calculation; meets I1, I3, and I4. Participant health status not specified in abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed. Include for full-text review to verify healthy participants and other details.

fMRI study in English reporting Stroop (executive function) activations and including healthy control subjects; however it also includes TBI patients and abstract does not confirm extractable healthy-only activation data — full text needed to confirm eligibility.

Abstract describes an English peer-reviewed fMRI study in healthy human participants examining working memory/central executive (executive function) tasks (operation/reading span, dual-task). No exclusion criteria are met.

The sample consists of Parkinson's disease patients (clinical population), not healthy adults. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (English peer-reviewed), I3 (fMRI), I4 (executive function task). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (Healthy human participants).
